 Assumptions
 A complete 52-week training program for Jonathan
 Priority order: Olympic weightlifting performance, hypertrophy, athleticism, longevity. Two flat barbell bench days
 every planned week; one targets low repetitions.

   Assumption / confirmed               Application
   constraint

   Failure scope - confirmed            Every conventional strength and hypertrophy WORK set ends at strict-form failure.

                                        mobility remain quality-limited. The operational definition is on page 2.

   Your starting point                  18-year-old male; 175 lb; 5 ft 9 in; four years of football strength training and power
                                        cleans, with less dedicated full-lift practice.

   Unknown measurements                 No conventional deadlift, strict press, full-clean or separate rack-jerk maximum is

   Health, equipment and                Assume pain-free training, a full gym, bumper plates and a platform. Barbell failure work
   technique                            requires correctly set safeties and competent spotting as described on page 2. A coach
                                        can check receiving and release; a no-coach regression is included.

   Availability and schedule            No time ceiling. Four weightlifting sessions; failure work follows B/D, normally
                                        Tuesday/Friday, optionally in a second visit. Whole sessions can roll around events
                                        (page 23); bench exceptions use pages 19-20. No competition date or weight class
                                        supplied.

   Physique                             Side delts and upper chest receive the greatest discretionary hypertrophy emphasis.
                                        Traps also receive an early dose trial in the first successful cycle (page 15). No glute
                                        isolation; retain useful full-depth squats.

   Pickup and alcohol                   Pickup basketball/football zero or about once weekly, unpredictably. Alcohol usually

                                        event is assumed harmless.

   Evidence and scope                   Targeted peer-reviewed review through 13 September 2026, including fresh exercise
                                        comparisons. Workout guidance only. Exact doses and scheduling are reasoned
                                        inference, not a tested optimal combined program. New selection/trial details: page 34.


  S = strong evidence for the stated finding; PE = partial evidence; RI = reasoned inference. These are narrative labels,
  not formal GRADE ratings. Direct trial findings and exact applications are separated on page 33. Your failure preference is a
  binding design constraint, not a finding that failure is superior. The plan seeks the best recoverable training within it; it cannot
  promise the same weightlifting outcome as an otherwise identical non-failure plan.




FAILURE WORK-SET EDITION / TRAINING ONLY / 13 SEP 2026 / REV 6                                                                           1

TRAINING PROGRAM


 Exactly what failure means
 Failure is the endpoint of a defined task. Keep range, position and rep standard fixed throughout each set. Use full
 comfortable ROM by default; only the preplanned page-34 calf trial uses a partial range. Operational rules: RI;
 terminology/fatigue evidence [49,50,52,53].

   Work type                        Endpoint and execution

   Stable machine / cable           Continue until another complete concentric repetition cannot be achieved with the
   work                             prescribed form. One unsuccessful controlled attempt may end the set. Return the
                                    resistance safely; no forced repetitions, drop sets, rest-pause extensions or assisted
                                    negatives.

   Free-weight strength work        Reach the last possible complete repetition with the prescribed form: no further valid rep in
                                    reserve. Re-rack when another attempt would require altered position or unsafe loss of
                                    control. If a rep stalls unexpectedly, the spotter/safeties end it immediately. Do not
                                    deliberately seek collapse.

   Technical limitation comes       If position fails before the target muscle does, stop and record TECH rather than claiming
   first                            muscular failure. Adjust load, exercise or setup next exposure. Pain, dizziness and loss of
                                    control are stop conditions, not successful failure endpoints.

   Barbell bench                    Use a full-thumb grip, stable feet/upper back and controlled chest touch with a brief pause.
                                    Set safeties to permit your normal range yet catch the bar if your arch relaxes; test with an
                                    empty bar. Use a competent spotter, especially on the low-rep day. No unprotected failed
                                    rep.

   Front / back squat               Use a rack with safeties just below your controlled bottom position and verify a safe exit with
                                    a light bar. End at the last repetition with intact depth, bracing and balance. Front-rack
                                    collapse or a folding back is technical termination, not a rep to fight through.

   Olympic and explosive            Snatch, clean & jerk, hang lifts, rack jerks and explosive snatch pulls use the stated short
   work                             sets and technical-effort ceilings. Never extend them to muscular failure. A miss triggers the
                                    quality rules, not another repetition to complete a quota.

   Warm-ups / mobility /            Preparation sets stay easy; jumps and sprints stop for quality loss; stretches stop at
   athletics                        mild-to-moderate tension. These are explicitly outside your confirmed failure requirement.

 Rep ranges choose the load; they do not replace the endpoint. A 3-5-rep failure set means selecting a load expected to
 permit 3-5 valid reps. If six are possible, do not falsely log failure at five; log the actual outcome and adjust the next exposure.
 Do not add another failure test to repair a load-selection error.


  Zero RIR on the final completed rep and an actually unsuccessful concentric attempt are related but not identical research
  conditions. The free-weight prescription uses the former when a failed attempt would be unsafe. No reserve target of 1-3 RIR
  is hidden inside conventional work sets.

TRAINING PROGRAM


 What the evidence changes
   Evidence and applicability        Programming consequence

   S: resistance training works      Broad evidence supports resistance training for strength and muscle growth [1]. This
                                     does not establish an optimal dose for a trained weightlifter also doing every work set to
                                     failure.

   PE: failure is not required       Older syntheses [55-58] and the 2026 review [10] do not establish failure as universally
                                     superior. The latter found a small dynamic-strength advantage for non-failure and no
                                     statistically clear hypertrophy/power difference. Your preference remains binding.

   PE: hypertrophy findings differ   Closer estimated proximity is associated with more growth [9]. Refalo 2024 [50] found
                                     similar quadriceps growth at failure and 1-2 RIR; Hermann 2025 [51] found modest
                                     advantages for some outcomes in single-set training. Definitions, doses and populations
                                     differ.

   PE: fatigue and velocity loss     Failure can increase acute fatigue [49,52]. Velocity-loss trials [48,59,60] show different
                                     strength, hypertrophy and athletic adaptations, but velocity loss is not an
                                     interchangeable measure of failure. No study supplies a universal recovery time or
                                     set-reduction percentage.

   S: volume trend / PE: heavy       More weekly work has diminishing returns [8]. In junior weightlifters, a middle amount of
   practice                          very heavy work outperformed the lowest/highest amounts on some outcomes [3];
                                     moderate total volume also performed well [2]. Neither minimal heavy practice nor
                                     frequent maxing is established as best.

   RI: the combined prescription     Four Olympic days, two failure days, the annual phases and every exact dose are
                                     individually monitored design choices. Studies have not tested this combination or
                                     proved it has zero cost to weightlifting performance.


 Use the hierarchy to make decisions
 Keep productive Olympic practice and the strength work that supports it first. Develop lagging muscles next, then
 athletic qualities, then health-only conditioning. Remove an identifiable interfering addition immediately; otherwise
 reverse lower-priority additions before cutting useful higher-priority work. RI.

  Research boundary: 13 September 2026; this is a targeted review, not a registered systematic review. The ACSM overview [1]
  searched through October 2024; newer studies are assessed separately. Page 33 separates direct findings from individual
  applications; page 34 records exercise comparisons. One-set failure research [51] has no multiple-set comparator; it cannot
  establish dose optimality.

 Split at the priority muscles - RI
 Preferred split when practical: visit 1 = Olympic work, squat, flat bench, incline and lateral raises (9 base failure
 sets). Visit 2, at least 3 h later = re-warm, upper rows 3-8, then lower block (13 sets). A single visit is acceptable
 while execution and full rests hold. The split changes neither weekly sets nor bench frequency; no recovery
 guarantee [4,11,49,52].
 Compare later-exercise first sets with their usual loads, session position and reps. Repeated loss of 2+ reps or poor
 execution despite full rest: trial the split for two exposures. If impairment persists, remove the latest addition or use
 pages 14/18. Address obvious impairment immediately. Day names are the normal calendar; whole-session deferral
 rolls the sequence (page 23). Omitted blocks from a completed session are not replayed; only bench is rescued
 separately (page 20). RI.

  shifting, preferably the normal spacing. This is a scheduling guardrail, not a recovery test. Keep bench after Olympic work and
  avoid relocating it immediately before a vulnerable priority session; page 20.

 When splitting sessions
 Before visit 2: 3-5 min easy movement, then the local ramps above. If idle for more than 15 minutes within a visit,

 rule, not a proven recovery interval. RI.

 Tempo and rest conventions
 Conventional work: approximately 2 seconds lowering, controlled transition and intent to lift promptly; a slow final rep
 is expected, but altered form is not. Calves pause 1 second at the bottom; bench pauses briefly on the chest. Do not
 add deliberately prolonged negatives or stretch holds to intensify failure. RI; [11,14-16,49].
 Rest is time after the set ends. Use 4-5 min for squat/low-rep bench, 3-4 min for moderate bench, incline and
 compound pulling, and 2-3 min for isolations. Longer is allowed if required to recover performance; a timer never
 forces an unready set. Exact durations are RI informed by rest and fatigue evidence [11,49,52].

  Warm-ups can reveal that a failure set should be omitted today. Do not use a failed warm-up as proof of readiness, and do not
  relabel an abandoned unsafe work set as a completed training target.
